tips.blacks: Controls the very darkest parts. Left deepens blacks; right lifts them toward gray and flattens depth.
tips.brightness: Mostly brightens or darkens mid-brightness areas, with less effect on the brightest and darkest ends.
tips.contrast: Increases the difference between light and dark. Right looks punchier; left looks softer and flatter.
tips.exposure: Brightens or darkens the whole photo at once—like changing how much light the camera captured.
tips.highlights: Controls overly bright areas (sky, window light). Left recovers detail and avoids blown whites; right brightens further.
tips.shadows: Controls darker areas. Right reveals detail in the dark; left deepens shadows for mood.
tips.toneMapper: How bright areas and color are mapped into what the screen can show. Basic is more literal and contrasty; Film is more film-like, with softer highlight roll-off and natural color—usually the better default.
tips.whites: Controls near-pure white peaks. Left pulls back clipped whites; right pushes highlights harder than Highlights alone.

tips.calibrationHue: Shifts the selected red/green/blue primary toward neighboring colors—for camera color fixes or a stylized look.
tips.calibrationSaturation: Makes the selected red/green/blue primary more or less vivid.
tips.calibrationShadowsTint: Adds magenta or green to dark areas. If shadows look green, move toward magenta (and the reverse).
tips.gradingBalance: Decides whether color grading leans more on darks or brights. Left favors shadows; right favors highlights.
tips.gradingBlending: How softly highlight, mid, and shadow color grades blend. Higher values look smoother.
tips.hue: Rotates every color together (e.g. green toward blue). Quick for looks or fixing a global cast.
tips.mixerHue: Shifts only the color you selected (e.g. reds) toward nearby hues; other colors stay put.
tips.mixerLuminance: Brightens or darkens only the selected color—e.g. lighter sky blues, darker leaf greens.
tips.mixerSaturation: Makes only the selected color more or less vivid—e.g. boost blues without touching skin.
tips.saturation: Makes all colors more vivid or more washed out together. Right = richer; left = closer to black and white.
tips.temperature: Warms (yellow/orange) or cools (blue) the photo. Cool indoor yellow casts; warm bluish cloudy shots.
tips.tint: Fixes magenta (pink-purple) or green casts. Skin too green → magenta; too pink → green.
tips.vibrance: Boosts muted colors first and is gentler on already-vivid colors and skin than Saturation.

color.wbPickerWgpuDisabled: WB Picker: Disable WGPU in Settings.

tips.blackLevel: Raises the darkest end. Right turns deep blacks gray and foggy; keep near 0 for solid blacks.
tips.darks: Brightens or darkens the “dark but not blackest” range—just above the deepest shadows.
tips.highlights: Controls the bright range: lower to keep sky detail; raise to brighten further.
tips.lights: Brightens or darkens the “bright but not whitest” range—just below the hottest highlights.
tips.shadows: Controls the dark range: right reveals detail; left deepens shadows.
tips.whiteLevel: Lowers the brightest end. Left softens harsh whites; keep near 0 to preserve bright peaks.

tips.blueYellow: Removes blue/yellow rainbow fringes on edges. Nudge until edges look clean.
tips.centre: Adds punch and clarity near the center of the frame, with less effect at the edges—good for subject focus.
tips.clarity: Makes shapes and texture look more defined. Right = clearer; too high can cause white halos.
tips.color: Removes colorful speckles (common in dark areas). Right = cleaner; avoid maxing out or colors look fake.
tips.dehaze: Right cuts haze for a clearer, punchier look; left adds soft fog. Use for misty scenes or a dreamy feel.
tips.luminance: Smooths grainy brightness noise. Right = cleaner; too high softens hair, fabric, and fine detail.
tips.redCyan: Removes red/cyan rainbow fringes on edges. Nudge until edges look clean.
tips.sharpness: Makes edges crisper. Right = sharper; left softens (nice for skin or a dreamy look).
tips.structure: Boosts fine texture (pores, leaves, fabric) more locally than Clarity. Too high can look gritty.
tips.threshold: How picky sharpening is. Higher values sharpen only strong edges, so flat areas pick up less noise.

tips.feather: How soft the vignette edge is. Higher values fade more gently into the center.
tips.glow: Adds a soft bloom around bright areas for a dreamy, backlit feel.
tips.grainAmount: How much film-like grain to add. Right = more grain; 0 = none.
tips.halation: Warm glow bleeding around bright spots, like old film—good for a vintage look.
tips.lensBlurAmount: How strong the background blur is. Higher = blurrier background and stronger subject pop.
tips.lensDiffusion: Adds soft glow inside the blur so highlights melt more dreamily.
tips.lightFlares: Adds lens flares and light streaks when facing a bright light—cinematic or sunny feel.
tips.midpoint: How far out the vignette starts. Higher = only the outer edges darken; center stays cleaner.
tips.roughness: How irregular the grain looks. Right = coarser/messier; left = finer and more even.
tips.roundness: Whether the vignette is more circular or follows the photo’s rectangular frame.
tips.size: How large each grain speck is. Right = coarser grains; left = finer.
tips.vignetteAmount: Darkens (or lightens) the edges to pull focus to the center. Right = darker edges; left can brighten corners.

tips.frequencySeparationFace: Overall face frequency-separation strength. When above 0, low/high bands can be adjusted separately.
tips.frequencySeparationBody: Overall body frequency-separation strength. When above 0, low/high bands can be adjusted separately.
tips.frequencySeparationFaceLow: Evens face tone and blotchiness; higher values look smoother.
tips.frequencySeparationFaceHigh: 0 keeps natural texture; positive softens pores/fine lines; negative boosts detail.
tips.frequencySeparationBodyLow: Evens body tone and blotchiness; higher values look smoother.
tips.frequencySeparationBodyHigh: 0 keeps natural texture; positive softens skin detail; negative boosts detail.
tips.hydratedSmoothingFace: Dewy face smoothing that softens blemishes while keeping natural glow.
tips.hydratedSmoothingBody: Dewy body smoothing that softens blemishes while keeping natural glow.
tips.evenSkinFace: Evens face tone depth and color cast for a cleaner complexion.
tips.evenSkinBody: Evens body tone depth and color cast for a cleaner complexion.
tips.whiteningFace: Brightens and softens face skin tone for gentle whitening.
tips.whiteningBody: Brightens and softens body skin tone for gentle whitening.
tips.aiBlemishRemoval: Detects and reduces spots and blemishes; higher values clean more aggressively.
tips.faceShineRemoval: Reduces oily facial highlights for a more matte, natural look.
tips.slimFace: Narrows the face along the contour for a slimmer look.
tips.bigEye: Enlarges the eye area for a brighter, more open look.
tips.eyeWhiteBrighten: Brightens the sclera for cleaner, more awake-looking eyes.
tips.eyeRedness: Reduces visible red veins in the eye whites without changing the iris.
tips.lipstick: Adds lipstick color and saturation to the lips.
tips.blusher: Adds blush to the cheeks for a healthier flush.

processing.alwaysDecodeRawDesc: Force full RAW decoding for thumbnails instead of using embedded JPEG previews. Enable this if your thumbnails look different in color or contrast compared to the opened image.
processing.backendDesc: Select the graphics API. 'Auto' is recommended. May fix crashes on some systems.
processing.dynamicDesc: The editor renders the preview to match your display's actual pixel density. This ensures that every detail is represented with 1:1 pixel accuracy, providing maximum clarity when zooming and checking focus.
processing.highDpiDesc: Render previews at your screen's native {{dpr}}x physical pixel resolution. Produces the sharpest possible preview but uses significantly more memory.
processing.highDpiDescStandard: This setting only affects high-DPI displays. Your current display is standard resolution.
processing.imageCacheDesc: Maximum number of full-resolution images kept in RAM. Higher values make switching between recently edited images instant, but use significantly more memory.
processing.linuxCompatDesc: Force software compositing to work around GPU driver crashes. Nvidia GPUs already get a lighter, automatic workaround, so only enable this if you still experience crashes on launch or when opening images.
processing.livePreviewQualityDesc: Controls the resolution and compression of the image while dragging sliders. Lower quality significantly improves responsiveness.
processing.livePreviewsDesc: Update the preview immediately while dragging sliders. Disable this if the interface feels laggy during adjustments.
processing.mediumThumbnailResDesc: Resolution of the preview shown while full images load in the editor.

preprocessing.applyPreprocessingDesc: If enabled, the base color noise reduction and pre-sharpening above will also be applied to standard formats.
preprocessing.colorNrDesc: Applies a cross-bilateral filter early in the pipeline to remove chroma noise. Higher value = Stronger NR.
preprocessing.defaultNonRawTonemapperDesc: The tonemapper to apply to non-RAW images (e.g., JPEG, PNG).
preprocessing.defaultRawTonemapperDesc: The tonemapper to apply to RAW images.
preprocessing.highlightRecoveryDesc: Controls how much detail is recovered from clipped highlights in RAW files. Higher values recover more detail but can introduce purple artefacts.
preprocessing.linearRawDesc: Fixes color casts or pink tint in some DNG files. Controls how already processed LinearRAW data is interpreted.
preprocessing.sharpeningDesc: Applies gentle detail enhancement early in the pipeline. Higher value = More sharpening.
preprocessing.title: Image Preprocessing
preprocessing.tonemapperOverrideDesc: Force a specific tonemapper globally for all images, hiding the tonemapper switch from the adjustments panel.
preprocessing.appleRaw9Desc: Develop RAW files with Apple's Core Image RAW 9 decoder, which demosaics and denoises in one step on the Neural Engine. Requires macOS 27 or later and a supported camera; unsupported files automatically use the built-in decoder. Slower than the default decoder. Thumbnails are not affected.
preprocessing.enableAppleRaw9: Use Apple RAW 9 for RAW files

processing.previewResDesc: Determines the maximum resolution of the preview. Lower values significantly improve performance.
processing.renderScaleDesc: Scales the render resolution relative to your display. Lower values improve performance on high-resolution screens at the cost of some sharpness.
processing.restartRequired: Changes to the processing engine require an application restart to take effect.
processing.smallThumbnailResDesc: Resolution of thumbnails shown in the library grid.
processing.staticDesc: The editor renders the image at a fixed resolution. This mode is the fastest and most consistent, making it ideal for lower-end hardware where smooth performance is prioritized over pixel-perfect zoom.
processing.staticPreviewResDesc: Sets the resolution for static previews like crop mode, lens correction, and perspective tools. Does not affect the main editor preview.
processing.thumbnailResDesc: Determines the resolution of generated library thumbnails. Higher values produce sharper images during loading.
processing.title: Processing Engine
processing.wgpuDescAndroid: Bypasses browser encoding for instantly responsive live previews. (Disabled on Android: Native WGPU surface creation is currently not supported alongside the mobile webview.)
processing.wgpuDescLinux: Bypasses browser encoding for instantly responsive live previews. (Disabled on Linux: Tauri uses GTK for webviews, which conflicts with WGPU on the same X11 surface and causes flickering.)
processing.wgpuDescRecommended: Bypasses browser encoding for instantly responsive live previews. Highly recommended for performance.
processing.workerThreadsDesc: Number of parallel threads used to generate thumbnails. Higher values speed up library loading but use more CPU & RAM.

tagging.aiTaggingDesc: Enables automatic image tagging using an AI (CLIP) model. This will download an additional model and impact performance while browsing folders. Tags are used for searching a folder.
tagging.clearAiTagsDesc: This will remove all AI-generated tags from your .rrdata files in all active root folders. User-added tags will be kept.
tagging.clearAllTagsDesc: This will remove all AI-generated and user-added tags from your .rrdata files in all active root folders. Color labels will be kept.
tagging.customListDesc: If provided, the AI will ONLY use tags from this list, overriding XiuLeMe’s built-in list. Tagging still uses English vocabulary; Chinese UI shows translated labels and accepts Chinese search.
tagging.maxAiTagsDesc: The maximum number of tags to generate per image.
tagging.noCustomTags: No custom AI tags (Using built-in list)
tagging.shortcutsDesc: A list of tags that appear as one-click buttons in the tagging context menu.
tagging.title: Tagging

thanks.description: A huge thank you to the following projects that were very important in the development of XiuLeMe:

list.darktable: For some reference implementations that guided parts of this work.
list.depth: For the powerful monocular depth estimation model that enables the AI depth masking capabilities.
list.gpupixel: For the portrait beauty runtime that powers face thinning, eye enlargement, and makeup effects.
list.lama: For the powerful & simple image inpainting model, which enables content-aware fill and object removal.
list.lensfun: For its invaluable open-source library and comprehensive database for automatic lens correction.
list.libgphoto2: For the comprehensive camera communication library powering XiuLeMe's tethering and remote capture subsystem.
list.mediapipe: For face detection, landmark, and portrait segmentation models that support portrait analysis and protection paths.
list.mmpose: For RTMPose human pose estimation that powers body reshape features such as arm slimming.
list.crhd: For the CRHD-3K high-definition portrait retouching work that enables blemish removal, evening, and skin whitening.
list.negpy: For the inspiration behind the negative conversion logic.
list.nind: For providing AI models that power the AI noise reduction capabilities in XiuLeMe.
list.onnxruntime: For the high-performance local ONNX inference engine that powers masking, portrait, and denoising AI features.
list.opencv: For image pre- and post-processing in the native portrait engine.
list.rapidraw: For the open-source RAW editor this project builds upon, which established much of the architecture and core capabilities.
list.rawler: For the excellent Rust crate that provides the foundation for RAW file processing in this project.
list.sam2: For providing the foundation model used for the AI subject detection capabilities.
list.schp: For the human-parsing model that provides region assignment for body reshape features such as arm slimming.
list.spektrafilm: For the spectrally-based film emulation LUTs by Andrea Volpato, used to power XiuLeMe's built-in film emulations. Licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.
list.u2net: For providing the robust architecture used for the AI sky and foreground detection capabilities.
list.you: For using and supporting XiuLeMe. Your interest keeps this project alive and evolving.

thanks.title: Special Thanks
